AddCardToHandHandler Handles the AddCardToHand action, creating new card instances and adding them to a player's hand. AddResourceHandler Handles the AddResource action, increasing a player's available resources. ApplyStatusHandler Handles the ApplyStatus action, applying keyword status effects to units. BonusAttackHandler Handles the BonusAttack action, allowing units to attack multiple times or out of sequence. BuffStatsHandler Handles the BuffStats action, applying permanent attack and health bonuses to units. DealDamageHandler Handles the DealDamage action, applying damage to player heroes or units. DestroyUnitHandler Handles the DestroyUnit action, immediately removing units from the board regardless of health. DrawCardHandler Handles the DrawCard action, allowing players to draw cards from their deck. DrawFromDiscardHandler Handles the DrawFromDiscard action, allowing players to draw cards from their discard pile. GiveToOpponentHandler Handles the GiveToOpponent action, transferring a card from one player to another. HealHandler Handles the Heal action, restoring health to players and units. HealToFullHandler Handles the HealToFull action, restoring a unit's health to maximum. MakeAUnitHandler Handles the MakeAUnit action, creating token units on the board with various placement rules. ModifyGlobalBuffHandler Handles the ModifyGlobalBuff action, applying permanent stat bonuses to all units of a player. MoveRightHandler Handles the MoveRight action, moving units one lane to the right on the board. ReturnToHandHandler Handles the ReturnToHand action, moving units from the board back to their owner's hand. SacrificeUnitHandler Handles the SacrificeUnit action, voluntarily destroying a friendly unit for an effect. ShuffleDeckHandler Handles the ShuffleDeck action, randomizing the order of cards in a player's draw pile. SilenceHandler Handles the Silence action, removing abilities and status effects from units. SummonUnitHandler Handles the SummonUnit action, which places a unit card from hand onto the board. TutorCardHandler Handler for the TutorCard action, which allows a player to search their deck for a specific card.

api/CardGame.Core.Cards.Models.CardInsta.summary: Class CardInstance Namespace CardGame.Core.Cards.Models Assembly CardGame.Core.dll Represents an instance of a card in the game with mutable state such as damage taken and buffs. Each card instance is immutable and returns new instances when modified. public class CardInstance Inheritance object CardInstance Constructors CardInstance(int, int, CardDefinition) Initializes a new instance of the CardInstance class with default values. Properties AuraKeywords Gets the keywords applied to this card via auras from other units. CostReduction Gets the cost reduction applied to this card (immutable once set). CurrentStats Gets the current calculated stats of the card, accounting for buffs, damage, and silenced state. DamageTaken Gets the amount of damage this card has taken. Definition Gets the static definition of the card (base stats, effects, etc.). InstanceId Gets the unique identifier for this card instance. IsSilenced Gets a value indicating whether this card is silenced (ignores all buffs and keywords). MaxHealth Gets the maximum health of the card (base health + permanent buffs, ignoring damage taken). OwnerPlayerId Gets the ID of the player who owns this card. PermanentBuffs Gets the permanent stat buffs applied to this card. SuppressedKeywords Gets the keywords that have been temporarily suppressed on this card. Methods AddPermanentBuff(CardStats) Adds a permanent stat buff to the card and returns a new instance. Silenced cards cannot receive buffs. Heal(int) Heals the card and returns a new instance. MoveAndReset() Creates a new card instance with all state reset to default (except InstanceId, Owner, and Definition). Typically used when moving a card between zones. Silence() Silences the card, removing all buffs, keywords, and auras, and returns a new instance. SuppressKeyword(Keyword) Temporarily suppresses a keyword on the card and returns a new instance. TakeDamage(int) Applies damage to the card and returns a new instance. WithAuras(IEnumerable<Keyword>) Updates the aura keywords on the card and returns a new instance. WithCostReduction(int) Updates the cost reduction on the card and returns a new instance. WithDamage(int) Creates a new card instance with the specified total damage.

TargetSelectedEvent Represents an event that occurs when a player selects a target for an effect or ability. UnitDestroyedEvent Represents an event that occurs when a unit is destroyed by a game effect. UnitDiedEvent Represents an event that occurs when a unit dies. UnitSacrificedEvent Represents an event that occurs when a unit is sacrificed (destroyed by its owner for an effect). api/CardGame.GodotClient.InputController.title: Method _Process | CardGame Docs
api/CardGame.GodotClient.InputController.summary: Method _Process Namespace CardGame.GodotClient Assembly CardGame.GodotClient.dll _Process(double) Called on each idle frame, prior to rendering, and after physics ticks have been processed. delta is the time between frames in seconds. It is only called if processing is enabled for this Node, which is done automatically if this method is overridden, and can be toggled with Godot.Node.SetProcess(bool). Processing happens in order of Godot.Node.ProcessPriority, lower priority values are called first. Nodes with the same priority are processed in tree order, or top to bottom as seen in the editor (also known as pre-order traversal). Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationProcess notification in Godot.GodotObject._Notification(int). Note: This method is only called if the node is present in the scene tree (i.e. if it's not an orphan). Note: When the engine is struggling and the frame rate is lowered, delta will increase. When delta is increased, it's capped at a maximum of Godot.Engine.TimeScale * Godot.Engine.MaxPhysicsStepsPerFrame / Godot.Engine.PhysicsTicksPerSecond. As a result, accumulated delta may not represent real world time. Note: When --fixed-fps is enabled or the engine is running in Movie Maker mode (see Godot.MovieWriter), process delta will always be the same for every frame, regardless of how much time the frame took to render. Note: Frame delta may be post-processed by Godot.OS.DeltaSmoothing if this is enabled for the project. public override void _Process(double delta) Parameters delta double

api/CardGame.GodotClient.InputController.title: Method _UnhandledInput | CardGame Docs
api/CardGame.GodotClient.InputController.summary: Method _UnhandledInput Namespace CardGame.GodotClient Assembly CardGame.GodotClient.dll _UnhandledInput(InputEvent) Called when an Godot.InputEvent hasn't been consumed by Godot.Node._Input(Godot.InputEvent) or any GUI Godot.Control item. It is called after Godot.Node._ShortcutInput(Godot.InputEvent) and after Godot.Node._UnhandledKeyInput(Godot.InputEvent). The input event propagates up through the node tree until a node consumes it. It is only called if unhandled input processing is enabled, which is done automatically if this method is overridden, and can be toggled with Godot.Node.SetProcessUnhandledInput(bool). To consume the input event and stop it propagating further to other nodes, Godot.Viewport.SetInputAsHandled() can be called. For gameplay input, this method is usually a better fit than Godot.Node._Input(Godot.InputEvent), as GUI events need a higher priority. For keyboard shortcuts, consider using Godot.Node._ShortcutInput(Godot.InputEvent) instead, as it is called before this method. Finally, to handle keyboard events, consider using Godot.Node._UnhandledKeyInput(Godot.InputEvent) for performance reasons. Note: This method is only called if the node is present in the scene tree (i.e. if it's not an orphan). public override void _UnhandledInput(InputEvent @event) Parameters event InputEvent

api/CardGame.GodotClient.LineView._Ready.summary: Method _Ready Namespace CardGame.GodotClient Assembly CardGame.GodotClient.dll _Ready() Called when the node is "ready", i.e. when both the node and its children have entered the scene tree. If the node has children, their Godot.Node._Ready() callbacks get triggered first, and the parent node will receive the ready notification afterwards. Corresponds to the Godot.Node.NotificationReady notification in Godot.GodotObject._Notification(int). See also the @onready annotation for variables. Usually used for initialization. For even earlier initialization, Godot.GodotObject.GodotObject() may be used. See also Godot.Node._EnterTree(). Note: This method may be called only once for each node. After removing a node from the scene tree and adding it again, Godot.Node._Ready() will not be called a second time. This can be bypassed by requesting another call with Godot.Node.RequestReady(), which may be called anywhere before adding the node again. public override void _Ready()

api/CardGame.GodotClient.html.summary: Namespace CardGame.GodotClient Classes BotCoordinator Manages the AI's turn execution flow within the Godot scene tree. Handles visual delays (for better UX), runs AI calculations on background threads to avoid freezing the UI, and dispatches the chosen commands back to the main thread. CardSlot Represents a visual container slot in the Deck Editor where a card can be dropped. Handles drag-and-drop detection and holds a reference to the displayed card. CardView Controls the visual representation of a single card in the game UI. Handles rendering card data (stats, text, art), input interactions (hover, click), and visual states (highlighting, selection). ChoiceModal UI Component responsible for displaying modal choices to the player. Supports both text-based options (buttons) and card selection grids (tutor). DeckEditor Manages the deck building interface, allowing players to create, edit, and save card decks. Handles the visualization of the card library, the current deck slots, and file I/O operations. DeckSelection Manages the Deck Selection screen where players can view, create, edit, and delete their custom decks. Handles scanning the file system for deck files and dynamically generating the UI list. GameBootstrap The main entry point and orchestrator for the gameplay scene in Godot. Responsible for initializing the core GameEngine, connecting UI and Input systems, and managing the main game loop (updates, turns, and game over states). GameDeckSelector Manages the deck selection screen before a match starts. Allows the player to choose their own deck (Left Click) and the bot's deck (Right Click). Features a custom SDF shader for visual feedback on selection states (Player, Bot, or Both). GameSession A persistent Singleton (Autoload) that stores global game data across scene transitions. Used to pass selected deck configurations from the Menu scenes to the Gameplay scene. This node persists throughout the application lifecycle. HeroPortrait Visual component representing a player's hero. Displays Health, Resources (Blood), and the Avatar image. Handles interactions like targeting the hero with spells and receiving dropped cards. InputController Controls player input and translates it into game commands. Manages input states (Idle, Targeting, Pending), card interactions, and mulligan phase. Acts as the bridge between the UI events and the Game Engine. LibraryCardEntry Represents a single card entry in the Deck Editor's library list. Displays the card visual and provides buttons to add or remove copies from the deck. LineView Visual controller for a single board lane (Line). Manages the placement of Enemy units (Top) and Player units (Bottom). MainMenu Controls the Main Menu scene, handling navigation to gameplay, deck editing, and providing global settings controls (like music). UIManager Manages the entire visual presentation of the gameplay scene. Acts as the View layer, rendering the GameState and handling UI interactions.
